description: Boeing 737-277 Advanced, MSN 22650, built for Ansett as VH-CZR. Later N183AW with America West, then A6-AVA, UP-B3702 and YA-GAB with operators in the United Arab Emirates, Kazakhstan and Afghanistan, latterly ZS-BIL with Gryphon Airlines in South Africa. Moved from OR Tambo to Hoedspruit by road in May 2019 over nine days and across three provinces because a retired airliner cannot be flown into a bush estate. Now fitted out as six hotel cabins. Build date: the hotel's own account calls it a 39-year-old airframe in 2019, an aviation feature gives October 1981; 1981 used. The construction number 806 quoted in that feature is the Boeing line number, not the MSN.

Boeing 727-191, built 2 June 1967 as N7273F for Frontier Airlines, later Braniff, then the Burlington Northern and Santa Fe Railway Company, then Dart and DSTS, and finally the Government of Djibouti as a presidential and VIP aircraft as J2-KBA until 2012. Stored at AeroNeXus at Johannesburg from September 2012 before moving to Hoedspruit, where it is fitted out as three VIP cabins. The hotel's own website calls it a Boeing 727-300, which is not a real variant; airhistory and airliners photo records confirm the 727-191. The construction number 418 quoted in an aviation feature is the line number and the MSN was not confirmed, so it is omitted.
